observations: NYSE identity/tradability validated in current packet.
SEC Q2 earnings release and 10-Q directly close the prior primary-financial-lineage gap; issuer operating sources are separated from independent market evidence and duplicate origins are collapsed.
risks: Operating/capacity claims remain issuer-heavy outside SEC-filed financials.
contradictions: Revenue and operating margin improved while quarterly and first-half cash conversion deteriorated materially year over year.

observations: Q2 revenue $3.4B grew 10.9% YoY; operating margin improved to 6.1% from 5.3%; backlog was $57.3B and awards $6.7B.
Q2 operating cash flow was -$31M and free cash flow -$150M versus +$823M/+730M a year earlier; six-month operating cash use was $421M.
Long-lead carrier funding, shipbuilding automation and mission/autonomy work support durable demand and bottleneck relevance, but labor/supplier/schedule execution remains material.
risks: Weak near-term cash conversion despite margin improvement
contradictions: Income-statement momentum and backlog strength coexist with weak cash conversion.

thesisQuality.basis: $57.3B backlog, $6.7B Q2 awards and carrier long-lead funding demonstrate durable demand; execution/cash conversion prevent exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue +10.9% and operating margin +80 bps support strong operating trend, offset by sharply negative Q2 and first-half cash conversion.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current independent market evidence supplies price/earnings context but not rare asymmetry; conservative mixed/balanced band retained.

catalystScore.basis: Raised shipbuilding guidance, carrier long-lead award and automation programs provide multiple source-supported medium-term catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Management raised guidance while disclosing cash-conversion pressure; adequate transparency and execution evidence, but cost/schedule risks remain.

alignment2036.basis: Nuclear-carrier and naval shipbuilding capacity plus autonomy/automation are foundational defense-industrial capabilities with long-duration demand.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Core shipbuilding plus mission/autonomy capabilities provide several demand channels, though U.S. government concentration remains high.

bottleneckControl.basis: Specialized U.S. nuclear-carrier/shipyard capacity has long lead times and high qualification/switching barriers.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Large backlog and multiple naval/mission programs support resilience, tempered by government concentration and execution sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.basis: Nuclear-carrier and complex naval shipbuilding require specialized facilities, labor and qualification that are difficult to replace quickly.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Long-lead material funding improves planning, but disclosed labor/supplier and schedule dependencies remain meaningful.

pricingPower.basis: Operating margin improved despite execution pressures, supporting some economic capture, but government contracting and cash conversion constrain evidence of durable pricing power.

riskEvidence.basis: Material labor/supplier, schedule, government-concentration and cash-conversion risks coexist with strong backlog and strategic demand.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC-filed financials plus issuer contract/capacity evidence and independent market context cover all score components; issuer concentration and unresolved cash-conversion tension prevent higher confidence.

scoreRecord.thesis: HII controls scarce U.S. naval shipbuilding capacity with durable backlog and modernization catalysts; upside depends on converting demand and automation into throughput, margins and cash.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Execution and cash conversion can lag backlog and revenue because labor, suppliers, schedules and government program concentration constrain realization.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Evidence of shipbuilding throughput/margin and operating/free-cash conversion improvement against raised FY26 guidance.
